Title: Miniature Inverted-Repeat Transposable Elements: Small DNA Transposons That Have Contributed to Plant MICRORNA Gene Evolution
Abstract: The majority of Type <m>II</m> TEs detected in <m>plant</m> nuclear genomes are <m>nonautonomous</m> <m>elements</m>, which have only retained the minimal sequences required to continue to be recognized as TEs, as they are either <m>truncated</m> derivatives of once <m>autonomous</m> <m>DNA</m> transposons or they continue to harbor stretches of terminal repeat sequences that share enough similarity with the termini of <m>autonomous</m> <m>elements</m> to enable their recognition and <m>transposition</m> via the cut-and-paste mechanism of movement.

Title: Atypical epigenetic and small RNA control of degenerated transposons and their fragments in clonally reproducing Spirodela polyrhiza
